title: Man. Post. Cap. IV: GAR 2 — separability / fidelium
pass_a_gloss: GAR. 2. Those things are not one and the same which in the thing itself can be separated. But someone can violate the law who nevertheless will not for that reason in act be deprived of his habitual justice, which is clear from the example of the faithful, who from time to time sin, and yet are not deprived of that justice which God by his Spirit has wrought in their hearts.
pass_b_english: Garissoles' second reason. Things that can really be separated are not one and the same. Someone may break the law and still not, in the act, lose habitual righteousness—as the faithful show, who sin from time to time yet keep the righteousness God works in their hearts by his Spirit.
source_text: GAR. 2. Ea non sunt unum & idem, quae reapse possunt separari. Atqui potest aliquis violare legem, qui tamen propterea justitia sua habituali actu non privabitur, quod patet exemplo fidelium, qui subinde peccant, nec tamen privantur ea justitia, quam Deus spiritu suo in ipsorum cordibus operatus est.

lemmas.gloss: to be separated in the thing itself
by the example of the faithful

choices.choice: separability + faithful who sin without losing habitual justice
